newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in moderate trade on Monday, dealers said.

Most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. June construction spending data, which are forecast to show an increase of 1.1 percent compared with a 1.8 percent fall reported in May, they said.

"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning on some position adjustments in term rates. Some traders are waiting for tonight's release of the construction spending figures, for more clues to market direction," a local dealer said.
"But unless the numbers are way off market expectations, I don't think there will be much impact," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Monday/Tuesday, Tuesday/Wednesday and week-fixed were unchanged from last Friday's common 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent, respectively.

Among longer dates, one-month rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, three-months was unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16, nine-months rose 1/16 point to 5-7/8 5-3/4 and twelve-months was unchanged at 5-15/16 5-13/16 percent.
